html:
SMTO-EXE-0206 — SMTO doesn't know if your new PDF file was saved

GUID: b97a56fb-5753-5621-a150-c87c101ca96a
Slug: pdf-outcome-unknown
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • SMTO lost track of the PDF action partway through. The new PDF or images may already have been saved even though no success was reported. Your original PDF was never overwritten.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Artifacts from this run and look for the new PDF or page images from this request. The action may have finished and saved its result even though SMTO didn't hear back.
  2. If you asked SMTO to save to a specific file name or folder, check that location on the Gateway computer too. Results saved to a name you chose go there instead of the run's artifacts.
  3. If the file is there and opens correctly, use it. Only if nothing was saved, ask SMTO again in a new message. Repeating an action that already worked creates duplicates or fails because the name is taken.
  4. If this keeps happening, open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for that Gateway. An unstable connection to the Gateway computer is a common reason SMTO loses the reply.

What success looks like

  • You've confirmed whether the new file exists, and you have exactly one copy of it.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete files you haven't checked.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A PDF write lost its result after the Gateway may already have run it or published output (lost or invalid response, transport error, or failure after output changed).

What this means

  • A PDF write lost a valid response after possible execution or publication changed output before a later exception. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • A PDF write lost a valid response after possible execution or publication changed output before a later exception.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact intended output paths and run artifacts, matching them to source revisions and the original operation.

How to fix it

  • Do not replay the write. Inspect the run's artifact workspace (artifact-workspace://pdf-* bundles) and any explicit output_path on the selected Gateway for files from the original request, compare them with what was requested, and only then decide whether to issue a new request. Investigate the transport or Gateway failure recorded in the retained cause.
  • Inspect target artifacts before another operation. Do not replay an uncertain write.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect target artifacts before another operation. Do not replay an uncertain write.

How to verify the fix

  • Original publication is reconciled before another output-producing action.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
